messages.author: b3ca0c52e87f982f
messages.subject: fine tuning of my first ggplot2 plot
parts:
Dear all,

first of all, please excuse me for the possibly basic question I have
and the poor subject of the thread.

I'm currently starting to use ggplot2 and attempts to tune a plot for
publication. It is a scatter plot representing performance of control
participants vs. brain damaged patients, with a lm regression line for
controls only, along with a 95% prediction confidence interval and a
dotted line corresponding to a probability of 0.05 of the distribution
of predicting a new score on the basis of the lm.

The following code do almost what I want. I just would like to
(1) change the colours for the groups (control would be blue and
patient would be red)
(2) modify the legend in order to reflect that the regression line and
confidence intervals are computed only for the 'control' group
(current legend shows a regression line and dashed area for both
groups) and
(3) add the regression equation above the legend.

Any help would be appreciated. And thanks a lot for this beautiful
package.

Regards,

Matthieu


## CODE:
library(ggplot2)

# generate some data
# group is a two level factor 'control' for normal participants;
'patient' for brain-damaged people
# the effect of the lesion is simulated in y by setting subtracting 2
on the 'y' value
x <- rnorm(100)
group <- factor(rbinom(x, size=1, p=0.2), labels=c('control',
'patient'))
y <- 1.3*x + 3 + ifelse(group=='control', 0, -2) + rnorm(x, sd=1)
final <- data.frame(group,x,y)

# initial plot
ppred <- qplot(x=x, y=y, colour=group, data=final)

# compute the regression for control subjects only
model <- lm(y~x, data=final, subset=group=='control')

# compute the predicted values for the confidence interval and the
dotted line, using predict
pred.grid <- with(final, expand.grid(
x=seq(min(x), max(x), length=101),
group='control'))
pred <- predict(model, newdata=pred.grid,interval=('prediction'))
pred <- data.frame(pred.grid,pred)
# select only the lower values of a confidence interval (level=0.9),
which corresponds to the lower 5%
pred$lwr.9 <- predict(model, newdata=pred,interval=('prediction'),
level=0.9)[,2]

# add layers to plot
ppred + geom_smooth(aes(y=fit, ymin=lwr, ymax=upr), data=pred,
stat='identity') + geom_line(aes(y=lwr.9), data=pred, linetype=2,
colour="grey40")

messages.subject: Re: fine tuning of my first ggplot2 plot
parts:
the colour is simple,

p <- last_plot() +
scale_colour_manual(values=c("#377EB8","#E41A1C")) # or "red" and
"blue", i prefer these

You can add an equation using Grid,

grob <- ggplotGrob(p)
grob <- addGrob(grob, textGrob(x = unit(0.9, "npc"), y = unit(0.7,
"npc"),label=expression(alpha^2),
gp = gpar(col = "red")))
grid.draw(grob)

but the legend seems more tricky. Hopefully someone will come up with
a solution.

HTH,

baptiste

parts:
Below is an ugly hack to remove the segment altogether from the legend
(hoping the colour coding would be enough). It's probably not
something to recommend, let's hope a better way is suggested to you,

library(ggplot2)

x <- rnorm(100)
group <- factor(rbinom(x, size=1, p=0.2), labels=c('control','patient'))
y <- 1.3*x + 3 + ifelse(group=='control', 0, -2) + rnorm(x, sd=1)
final <- data.frame(group,x,y)

# compute the regression for control subjects only
model <- lm(y~x, data=final, subset=group=='control')
# compute the predicted values for the confidence interval and the
# dotted line, using predict

pred.grid <- with(final, expand.grid(
x=seq(min(x), max(x), length=101),
group='control'))
pred <- predict(model, newdata=pred.grid,interval=('prediction'))
pred <- data.frame(pred.grid,pred)
# select only the lower values of a confidence interval (level=0.9),
# which corresponds to the lower 5%
pred$lwr.9 <- predict(model, newdata=pred,interval=('prediction'),level=0.9)[,2]
p <- ggplot(data = final, mapping = aes(x = x, y = y, fill=group)) +
geom_smooth(aes(y=fit, ymin=lwr, ymax=upr), data=pred, stat='identity') +

geom_line(aes(y=lwr.9), data=pred, linetype=2, colour="grey40")+
geom_point(aes(colour=group))+
scale_colour_manual(values=c("#377EB8","#E41A1C")) +
scale_fill_manual(values=c("#377EB8", NA))


GeomSmooth$draw_legend <- function (., data, params, ...)
{
data <- aesdefaults(data, .$default_aes(), list(...))
data$fill <- alpha(data$fill, data$alpha)
rectGrob(gp = gpar(col = NA, fill = data$fill))

}

p
# reload the default one
detach(package:ggplot2, unload=T)
library(ggplot2)

# p # usual behavior

OK, here's one I am having some trouble with .... excuse the length ....the idea
is to compare how Obama did and how Kerry did in different congressional districts,
using LM.

# FIRST, I SET UP THE DATA

library(foreign)
library(ggplot2)
origdata <- read.csv("c:/personal/dailykos/blackrepdem.csv")
state <- substr(origdata$district, 1, 2)
southern <- state == 'AL' | state == 'AR' | state == 'FL' | state == 'GA' | state == 'LA'|
state == 'MS' | state == 'NC' | state == 'SC'| state == 'TN' | state == 'VA'
party <- substr(origdata$Party,2,2)

testdata <- expand.grid(southern = c(TRUE, FALSE), Black = seq(0, 65, by = 10))

#NEXT, THE OBAMA EQUATION

ObamaRegionBlack <- with(origdata, ols(Obama~southern*Black))

Obamapredicted <- predict(ObamaRegionBlack, testdata)
Obamaprediction <- data.frame(cbind(testdata, Obamapredicted))

# AND A PLOT

plot2 <- qplot(data = Obamaprediction, Black, Obamapredicted, colour = southern,
main = "Obama vote predicted by region and pct Black.",
xlab = 'Percent Black',
ylab = 'Predicted Obama vote')

plot2 <- plot2 + geom_line() + aes(colour = southern) + scale_colour_manual(value = c("red", "blue"))


# SAME THING FOR KERRY
KerryRegionBlack <- with(origdata, ols(Kerry~southern*Black))

Kerrypredicted <- predict(KerryRegionBlack, testdata)
Kerryprediction <- data.frame(cbind(testdata, Kerrypredicted))

plot3 <- qplot(data = Kerryprediction, Black, Kerrypredicted, colour = southern,
main = "Kerry vote Kerrypredicted by region and pct Black.",
xlab = 'Percent Black',
ylab = 'Predicted Kerry vote')

plot3 <- plot3 + geom_line() + aes(colour = southern) + scale_colour_manual(value = c("red", "blue"))

# AND THOSE TWO ARE GOOD. JUST HOW I WOULD WANT THEM

# BUT TO COMBINE THEM?????? HERE'S WHAT I DID, BUT, WHILE IT'S OK IT ISN'T GREAT AT ALL
plot4 <- qplot(data = Kerryprediction, Black, Kerrypredicted, colour = southern,
main = "Kerry and Obama vote Kerrypredicted by region and pct Black.",
xlab = 'Percent Black',
ylab = 'Predicted Democratic vote',
ylim = c(30, 100))

plot4 <- plot4 + geom_line() + aes(colour = southern) + scale_colour_manual(value = c("red", "blue"))


plot4 <- plot4 + geom_abline(intercept = 49.42, slope = 0.682, colour = 'blue', linetype = 2)
plot4 <- plot4 + geom_abline(intercept = 49.42-13.88, slope = 0.682-.129, colour = 'red', linetype = 2)

Conceptually, you need to combine Obamaprediction and Kerryprediction
into a single data frame, adding a variable that differentiates
between the two, and using the same variable for the y axis. Then you
can do something like:

ggplot(both, aes(percent_black, prediction, colour = southern,
linetype = president)) +
geom_line()

(Assuming I'm guessing correctly what you want)
